question: What is the largest organ in the human body?
explanation: The skin covers the entire external surface of the body, making it the largest single organ by surface area and weight. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is the skin considered part of the body's primary defense system?

options.A: It produces white blood cells continuously
options.B: It digests harmful toxins entering the body
options.C: It blocks pathogens, chemicals, and physical injury
options.D: It pumps blood to destroy foreign bacteria

explanation: The skin acts as an unbroken physical barrier that stops germs and harsh environmental elements from entering internal tissues. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h1)

question: Where does active skin cell division take place in the outer layer (epidermis)?
explanation: Great try! The stratum basale is the lowest, busiest layer of the epidermis where fresh new skin cells are constantly born to replace the old ones. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h2)

question: When old skin flakes off after a minor scrape heals, which layer is mostly shedding?
explanation: Spot on! The stratum corneum is our outermost layer made of tough, dead cells that naturally flake off over time. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which skin layer contains the blood vessels, nerve endings, and collagen fibers?
explanation: The dermis is the vascularized middle layer of the skin that holds blood vessels, nerves, and tough connective tissue fibers. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h3)

question: What anatomical feature of the skin creates your unique fingerprints?

options.A: Dermal papillae interlocking beneath the surface
options.B: Friction of the outer skin rubbing against clothes
options.D: Adipose tissue buildup in the lower layer

explanation: You got it! Tiny wave-like bumps called dermal papillae push up from the dermis, creating the unique patterns we know as fingerprints. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary type of tissue found in the hypodermis?
explanation: The hypodermis is heavily populated by fat-storing adipose cells that provide insulation and cushion underlying structures. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is a major physiological function of the hypodermis?

options.A: Insulating the body against heat loss
options.B: Detecting fine touch and deep pain sensations
options.D: Secreting sweat to cool the skin surface

explanation: The layer of fat in the hypodermis acts as thermal insulation, helping to prevent excessive body heat loss to the environment. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h4)

question: Which skin gland secretes an oily substance called sebum?
explanation: Sebaceous glands produce sebum, an oily substance that lubricates and waterproofs the hair and skin. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a job of the ordinary sweat glands (eccrine glands)?

options.A: Excreting tiny amounts of body waste
options.B: Producing thick, smelly sweat in the armpits
options.C: Helping cool down the body through sweat evaporation
options.D: Releasing watery fluid onto the skin

explanation: Spot on! Armpit and groin sweat comes from apocrine glands, while your ordinary (eccrine) glands make watery sweat all over to keep you cool. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which vitamin is synthesized in the skin when exposed to sunlight?
explanation: Ultraviolet light helps convert cholesterol compounds in the skin into active vitamin D precursors necessary for bone health. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h6)

question: A patient has severe burns on 40% of their body. Which skin job will be seriously affected?
explanation: You got it! Since healthy skin is needed to make vitamin D from sunlight, extensive burns make this process very difficult. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary pigment responsible for protecting skin cell DNA from ultraviolet damage?
explanation: Melanin is produced by melanocytes to absorb UV radiation and shield the DNA in underlying skin cells from mutation. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h7)

question: What does your skin do when you step into a cold environment?

options.A: Blood vessels in the skin widen to let heat out
options.B: Sweat glands release extra cooling fluid
options.D: Blood vessels in the skin narrow to hold in body heat

explanation: Well done! When it's cold, your blood vessels squeeze shut near the surface to keep your warm blood safely around your inner organs. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h7)
